newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO STOCKS SEEN MIXED AMID CAUTIOUS MOOD.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO STOCKS SEEN MIXED AMID CAUTIOUS MOOD.

text.p: Trading in Tokyo stocks is expected to be mixed on Thursday amid a lack of strong incentives for buying or selling, brokers said.
On Wednesday, the benchmark Nikkei 225 average finished down 90.51 points or 0.47 percent at 19,008.60. Its September futures lost 70 points to 19,030.
Participants will be inclined to stay on the sidelines ahead of the announcement of several U.S. economic figures which could cause turbulence in the New York market, brokers said.

"Market participants will likely buy in the construction sector and other domestic demand-related issues following yesterday's announcement of the Mitsui group's support for Mitsui Construction's restructuring plan," said a broker at a major Japanese brokerage.

He also said, however, that some institutional investors would take profits on high-tech issues, whose prices have been rising in recent sessions, ahead of mid-term book-closings at the end of September.
In other indices, the TOPIX index nudged up 2.39 points or 0.16 percent to 1,480.26. The Nikkei 300 average was up 0.35 point or 0.12 percent at 289.52.
Among chip equipment makers, Tokyo Electron Ltd rallied 350 yen to 7,670 yen, while Advantest Corp was up 500 yen at 12,300.
Other high-tech firms that manufacture chip equipment also gained ground, with Nikon Corp up 140 yen at 2,460 and Canon Inc up 120 yen at 3,670.
On Wednedsay, Applied Materials' shares surged after it reported earnings far exceeding Wall Street's expectations.
Another focus of the market was the construction sector.

Shares of Mitsui Construction Co Ltd were bid-only throughout the morning session, after the company announced on Wednesday that other firms in the Mitsui group would support its restructuring programme.
At midday, Mitsui Construction shares were bid-only at 195 yen, after last trading at 170 yen on Wednesday. The TSE suspended trade in the shares on Wednesday afternoon.
Other construction firms facing financial troubles declined in the morning, however, after briefly rising in a knee-jerk reaction to the Mitsui news.
Shares of Hokkaido Bank Ltd rose and those of Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd fell after a newspaper report that they were considering delaying a planned merger.
Hokkaido Bank's president said after the report, however, that the bank was not considering such a delay.
Hokkaido Bank shares were up one yen at 137 and Hokkaido Takushoku shares were down two yen at 115.
By sector, gainers were led by trading houses, fisheries, precision instruments, and electric equipment. The major losers were warehousing, mining, oil, and brokerages.
